== Problem ==
Two integers are inserted into           the list <imath>3, 3, 8, 11, 28</imath> to double its range. The mode and median remain unchanged. What is the maximum possible sum of the two additional numbers?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 56 \qquad \textbf{(B) } 57 \qquad \textbf{(C) } 58 \qquad \textbf{(D) } 60 \qquad \textbf{(E) } 61</imath>

==Solution 1 ==
To double the range, we must find the current range, which is <imath>28 - 3 = 25</imath>, to then double to: <imath>2(25) = 50</imath>. Since we do not want to change the median, we need to get a value less than <imath>8</imath> (as <imath>8</imath> would change the mode) for the smaller, which will be <imath>7</imath>. This fixes <imath>53</imath> for the larger value. Anything less than <imath>3</imath> is not beneficial to the optimization because you want to get the largest range without changing the mode. So, taking our optimal values of <imath>7</imath> and <imath>53</imath>, we have an answer of <imath>7 + 53 = \boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 60}</imath>.

~apex304, SohumUttamchandani, wuwang2002, TaeKim, CrystalFlower, CHECKMATE2021, lazypanda5050
